subject: On-prem: nightly-batch tail-latency spike + 5xx amplification — remediation plan & exec sync
messages:
From: ops+alerts@clientcorp.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: adam.tan@clientcorp.com, sarah.nguyen@clientcorp.com
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: [ALERT] ClientCorp on-prem nightly batch: p95 jump and 502 amplification

Hey team,

Monitoring flagged a persistent p95 latency increase during ClientCorp's nightly batch (02:00 window UTC) starting 2027-06-18 02:04 UTC. We also saw a correlated spike in 502/503 responses from the model nodes — error rate ~4% during the window (baseline <0.2%). This recurred tonight.

Attached are the collected p95/p99 time series and a short tail-sample of request IDs (clientcorp_nightly_p95_logs_20270619.log). We're scheduling a maintenance window if needed but would like Redwood to triage first — this batch is critical for their billing reconciliation process.

Thanks,
ClientCorp Ops Alerting
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: ops+alerts@clientcorp.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 09:01:12 -0700
Subject: Re: [ALERT] ClientCorp on-prem nightly batch: p95 jump and 502 amplification

Thanks for the heads up, Sarah / team.

Laura — can you dig into the logs and confirm whether this looks like KV cache ejects or a decode bottleneck at the node level? I want a short first-pass analysis in the next 60 minutes so we can decide: immediate mitigation (increase concurrency / enable fallback model variant) vs scheduled maintenance.

Looping in Marissa for customer comms if we need an exec sync.

— Irene
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 09:41:37 -0700
Subject: Re: [ALERT] ClientCorp on-prem nightly batch: p95 jump and 502 amplification

Initial findings (quick triage):

- Repro window matches the nightly batch start (02:00 UTC).
- Node-level logs show repeated evictions in the KV cache at ~02:06 UTC for the hot shard set. The eviction count rises sharply right before the p95 spike.
- Concurrently, we see kernel-level SIGPIPE on one worker for ~45s; after that workers return 502 until requests get routed off the node. The pattern looks like: KV cache cold -> heavier beam-search work -> increased memory pressure -> worker-level failure -> upstream 502 amplification.

Attached: clientcorp_nightly_p95_logs_20270619.log and kvcache_kerneldump_snippet.txt.

Recommended immediate mitigations (can be applied without redeploy):
1) Increase kvcache.max_entries from 1.2M -> 1.6M for the hot shard set (config patch attached below).
2) Lower per-request beam_size temporarily from 6 -> 4 to reduce peak decode working set for batch window.
3) Route 20% of nightly-batch traffic to the smaller but stable model-variant (model-v1-compact) as a graceful fallback to absorb traffic during the mitigation.

If those are executed, we should monitor p95 and 5xx for three subsequent runs. If issues persist, we escalate to full node replacement + live kernel debug.

Config diff (suggested):
--- /etc/redwood/clients/clientcorp/config.yaml 2027-06-18
+++ /etc/redwood/clients/clientcorp/config.yaml 2027-06-19
@@
- kvcache:
-   max_entries: 1200000
+ kvcache:
+   max_entries: 1600000
@@
- model_params:
-   beam_size: 6
+ model_params:
+   beam_size: 4

— Laura
Principal SRE, Runtime
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation: ClientCorp nightly batch outage risk — exec sync request

Team,

Laura confirmed KV cache ejects leading to worker failures and 5xx amplification during ClientCorp's nightly window. This is high visibility (ClientCorp billing reconciliation) and the customer is watching. I propose we:

- Apply Laura's recommended mitigations as a hotpatch (kvcache bump + beam_size reduction + 20% fallback routing) to tonight's run.
- Prepare an exec-facing summary for ClientCorp and schedule a 30-minute sync with their CTO and our CRO/CS lead.
- Post-mitigation: collect three-run metrics and agree on a permanent config change or capacity bump.

Marissa: can your team handle customer comms and book the sync (preferably <24 hours)? Jonas / Marcus: please approve the hotpatch and confirm rollback steps.

— Irene
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: sarah.nguyen@clientcorp.com, adam.tan@clientcorp.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 10:32:15 -0700
Subject: Redwood update: action plan for nightly-batch latency and 5xxs (urgent)

Sarah / Adam — thanks for surfacing this. We're treating it as a priority. Short plan: 

1) Tonight (02:00 UTC run): we will apply a non-disruptive hotpatch that increases KV cache allocation for your hot shard set, temporarily reduces beam_size, and routes 20% of traffic to a compact model variant to lower peak memory use. No service restart required; we will monitor closely.
2) We will run the mitigation on your next three nightly batches and share per-run p95/p99 and 5xx numbers within 2 hours of each run.
3) We propose a 30-minute executive sync tomorrow to review findings and permanent options (config vs capacity). Can you do 10:00 AM PT tomorrow (Sun, 2027-06-20)?

Attachments: nightly_batch_runbook_v2.pdf (runbook + rollback steps), logs referenced earlier.

If you prefer, we can schedule the sync earlier — let me know.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
